newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks stage sharp late recovery on Dow.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks stage sharp late recovery on Dow.

text.p: Mexican blue-chip stocks turned around in late trade to end sharply up Monday after slumping for most of the session along with Wall Street.
"It was nothing other than the Dow (Jones industrial average), and dealers took advantage of (cheap) prices to buy ahead of first-quarter earnings reports," a floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index ended up 34.19 points, or 0.91 percent, at 3,798.65 after sliding as low as 3,707.65 in midafternoon trading.
Trading also recovered from its recent doldrums, with volume at 89.97 million shares.
The Dow closed up 60.21 points at 6,451.90 points.
Analysts drew attention to the fact the IPC rebounded at just above a psychological barrier of 3,700 points.

"It was very important the IPC stayed above the 3,700-point mark. Despite our recent falls, returns on the bourse for the year to date are still in positive turf, as opposed to Wall Street," said Esteban Rojas, an analyst with the Arka brokerage in Mexico City.
Rojas was cautious, however, regarding reaction on the market to forthcoming key U.S. economic data and whether they augured further interest rate hikes to curb overheating.
Expected increases in domestic interest rates at Tuesday's primary Treasury bill auction could also pour cold water on the market, traders said.

Money market traders said they forecast increases of up to one percentage point in bellwether 28-day Cetes, or Treasury bill, rates at Banco de Mexico's weekly auction of government securities Tuesday.
A late rebound by telecommunications company Telmex had the most effect on the market's late recovery.

Telmex L shares ended up 22 centavos (3 cents) at 16.06 pesos ($2.03), up from a session low of 15.70 pesos ($1.98). Telmex American Depository Receipts, meanwhile, ended unchanged at $40, after recovering from a low of $39.625.
Key financial and construction stocks declined sharply on expectations they would post poor first-quarter earnings.

Construction firm Tribasa ended down 1.20 pesos (15 cents) at 23.50 pesos ($2.97). Financial stock GFB B shares fell 11 centavos (1 cent) to 2.47 pesos (31 cents), while counterparts Serfin A shares closed down 11 centavos (1 cent) to 2.01 pesos (25 cents).
The broad market did not match the late upswing in blue chips and ended mixed. Of a total of 108 stocks traded, decliners outnumbered gainers by 47 to 31.
